query: I know it's only seven in the morning but this was the best time to reach you.
I'll try you again tonight around ten thirty since you're hard to catch.
I understand you have a lawyer handling this, but I'd rather work it out with you directly.
If I don't hear back I'll reach you at your office tomorrow afternoon.
You gave us permission on our last call to reach you at this hour.
I see you sent a written request that we stop contacting you, but I'm calling about the balance anyway.
I'm reaching out one final time only to let you know we are ending our collection efforts on this account.
I spoke with your sister yesterday and explained what you owe on this account.
I discussed the debt with your attorney, which you authorized.
We only email addresses that the creditor confirmed with you beforehand.
Every electronic message we send includes a simple way for you to opt out.
I just need to confirm your home address and the phone number where you live.

I've called your brother three times this week trying to get your address.
I'm going to keep calling you until you get tired of hearing from me.

The calls that never connected don't count toward the frequency limit.
If you don't pay we'll send someone to your house to collect it in person.

Your name is going on our published list of consumers who refuse to pay.
I called four times today and hung up each time without saying who I was.
You opted out of text messages but I'm sending you the payment link by text anyway.
You texted us first, so I'm replying to you the same way.
Everything I have told you about this account today is completely accurate.
I'm calling from the federal collections office about your outstanding debt.
I'm an attorney and I've been assigned to handle your case personally.
If you don't pay today a warrant will be issued and you could be arrested.
We are filing a lawsuit against you next week if this isn't resolved.
This is National Legal Services calling, though that isn't the name our business operates under.
This is an attempt to collect a debt and any information obtained will be used for that purpose.
As I mentioned when we first spoke, this communication is from a debt collector.
There is a twenty five dollar processing fee added on top of the balance for paying by phone.
Just send me a check dated three weeks out and I'll hold onto it until then.
We went ahead and deposited your postdated check a week before the date on it.
We will repossess your vehicle if the balance isn't paid by Friday.
We mailed you a postcard last week about the outstanding balance.
I sent you a public message on social media about this debt since you weren't answering.
The limitations period on this account has already expired.
We are going to take you to court over this debt even though it is time barred.
We reported this account to the credit bureaus before ever contacting you about it.

We will file the action to enforce the lien in whichever county is most convenient for us.
We sent your validation notice within five days of our first contact with you.
The itemization date shown on your notice is the date of your last payment.
Your validation period runs for thirty days from when you received the notice.
Your notice lists the creditor's name and the amount owed as of the itemization date.
The notice includes the dispute prompts and the mailing addresses for both of us.
You disputed this in writing, but we are continuing to collect while we look into it.
You asked for the name of the original creditor and I will mail that to you.
Because you disputed the debt, we will send you verification before collecting further.
We keep records showing compliance for three years after our last activity on an account.

Your state's collection law doesn't apply to us because we follow the federal rule.
I'm not a debt collector, I work directly for the company that originally extended the credit.
